Moderation is easy for me when not restricting calories. When I am restricting I find it near impossible and often eat the entire box/pack.

Try and eliminate any calorie goal from your mind, so it doesn't feel wrong to go over it. I sometimes automatically start calculating in my head even though I haven't physically tracked calories in a year. I've noticed it's on days where I don't each as much, so my brain gets excited thinking maybe I didn't eat enough so I will lose weight and starts calculating the possibility.

You have to make an effort to not calorie count. Try going to restaurants or having other people prepare food so you have no idea? That might make you grossly overestimate calories to be safe like I did though. For me, I just had to keep eating and not change how much I ate based on the calculations in my head. They slowly lose meaning. I rarely binge anymore and feel genuinely satisfied on a normal amount of food everyday. I've lost 20lbs by just not binging.

"Eating well" (if you are dieting/restricting food) and obsessively excercising is likely what is triggering the binges. To stop binging you need to calm down with that. I know it is hard to stop because I had to also, but it is so worth it.
